clue.text: Regularly, man bursts on to peak programme

blocks.note: the peak is the top
oft is an old word for often
a man is a he
a balloon pops when it bursts

explanation.surface: A man bursts on to the top of a mountain at regular intervals, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on to' tells you the rest is attached to the peak, which comes first. Top of the Pops was the long-running BBC weekly chart music show.
explanation.definitionFit: Top of the Pops was a British television show, so it is a programme by name.

clue.text: Bird falls on rodent with energy to test strength

blocks.note: a tit is a small songbird
a rat is a rodent
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A bird of prey drops on a rat to see how strong it is.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the bird falls on, so sits above, the rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemists titrate a solution to measure its concentration, which is its strength.

clue.text: Why Italian duke sat up

blocks.note: perché is Italian for why
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: Someone asks why an Italian aristocrat sat up straight.
explanation.definitionFit: Perched means sitting up high, like a bird on a branch.

clue.text: From hole stared out seeing skylight

indicators.note: letters put out of their places are scrambled

blocks.note: being in a hole is being in a fix, a predicament
the letters of this word rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a hole gazes up at a window in the roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skylight' is not a roof window here but a light in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed star is a star in the night sky, which is literally a light in the sky.

clue.text: Creature smaller than whippoorwill?  Yes and no

indicators.note: a word that is smaller than another can sit wholly within it

blocks.note: the letters run inside this bird's name
surface padding: a wry answer to the question, true of the word but not the animal

explanation.surface: A quiz question asking whether one animal is smaller than a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yes and no' is the joke: the word is smaller than the bird's name that contains it, but the beast itself is enormous. A whippoorwill is a small North American nightjar.
explanation.definitionFit: A hippopotamus is a large African animal, so a creature.

clue.text: Expect platter but no coffee – it's on order

indicators.note: but no means the following word is taken away from the one before

blocks.note: taken as written
a latte is a milky coffee
an edict is an official order

explanation.surface: A diner expects a platter of food but no coffee, since that is already ordered.
explanation.walkthrough: A latte is a milky coffee. 'it's on' places what remains of the dish above the order in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To predict is to foresee or anticipate, which is to expect something to happen.

clue.text: Always wrapped at first in a cloak of obscurity?  Not a feature of our website

definitions.text: Not a feature of our website

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before
in puts the preceding pieces inside the cloak that follows

blocks.note: ay (or aye) is an old word for always
the first letter of this word
a pall is a dark covering that obscures, like a pall of smoke

explanation.surface: A query about something kept permanently wrapped in mystery, then a pointed remark about the newspaper's own site.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian, where this ran, famously keeps its website free to read with no subscription barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A paywall blocks online articles unless you subscribe, which the Guardian's website deliberately does not do.

clue.text: Tolerant principle in assize: a lifer released

indicators.note: letters released from their order are free to fall into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: At a criminal court session, a prisoner serving life is let go under a lenient policy.
explanation.walkthrough: An assize was a former English criminal court session.
explanation.definitionFit: Laissez-faire is the doctrine of leaving things alone without interfering, a permissive or tolerant principle.

clue.text: Roman fighter gives Daisy one kiss

blocks.note: an aster is a daisy-like flower
I is the Roman numeral one
X is the kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A Roman gladiator gives a girl called Daisy a single kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman fighter' reads as a fighter who is Roman, but means one who fights Romans.
explanation.definitionFit: Asterix is the comic-book Gaul who spends his adventures battling the occupying Romans.

clue.text: Drunk – on power, that is. Like some potatoes?

blocks.note: P is the symbol for power
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
potatoes have eyes, the buds on their skin

explanation.surface: Someone drunk on power, followed by a sly question about potatoes.
explanation.walkthrough: This clue pairs with 11, which has the same definition and the same potato question.
explanation.definitionFit: Pie-eyed is informal slang for very drunk.

clue.text: Manifest reluctance as fiery type set out to claim payment

indicators.note: set out suggests arranging, so the letters are laid out afresh
to claim something is to take it in, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: a dragon breathes fire
the letters of this word rearranged
a fee is a payment

explanation.surface: Someone shows unwillingness as a hothead sets out to demand money.
explanation.definitionFit: To drag one's feet is an idiom for delaying deliberately, showing reluctance.

clue.text: Drunk a little soup. Like some potatoes?

indicators.note: a little of the word means just a small taste of it, its opening letter

blocks.note: the first letter of this word
potatoes are often served mashed

explanation.surface: Someone drinks a little soup, then the same potato question as 9.
explanation.walkthrough: A twin of 9 across: same definition, same potato question, a different answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Smashed is informal slang for very drunk.

clue.text: In part of Japan, old family on holiday short of yen

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the following letter is dropped

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
kin are family
people on holiday are away
Y is the abbreviation for yen, Japan's currency

explanation.surface: An elderly family on holiday in Japan runs out of local money.
explanation.definitionFit: Okinawa is a Japanese prefecture and island group in the far south of the country.

clue.text: Do some editing, taking Imogen in last

indicators.note: a piece that takes something in holds it inside

blocks.note: the last part is the end
Imogen is the setter, so me

explanation.surface: An editor makes changes, leaving the setter's own contribution until the end.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter naming themselves means ME.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct it, which is a form of editing.

clue.text: Closed in a twinkling a drawer for small fruit

indicators.note: in places the following pieces inside the brief time

blocks.note: a door pushed to is closed
a mo is a moment, a twinkling
taken as written
a till is a cash drawer

explanation.surface: A cash drawer shuts in an instant on a little piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawer' is the drawer in a cash register, not an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: The tomatillo is a small green husked fruit related to the tomato, used in Mexican salsas.

clue.text: Taking pains to enjoy oneself at great speed, covering in this way first of several miles

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around, so one piece holds the next
first of points to the opening letter only

blocks.note: Mach one is the speed of sound
so means in this way
the first letter of this word
M is the abbreviation for miles

explanation.surface: Someone takes great trouble to enjoy themselves driving very fast for miles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking pains' is read literally: enjoying the taking of pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Masochism is the tendency to derive pleasure from one's own suffering.

clue.text: Some honours that won't give you the pip

definitions.text: Some honours that won't give you the pip

blocks.clueFragment: Some honours that won't give you the pip
blocks.note: surface reading: awards that won't annoy you, the pip being irritation

blocks.clueFragment: Some honours that won't give you the pip
blocks.note: setter's reading: top playing cards that carry pictures instead of suit symbols

explanation.walkthrough: In card games the honours are the top cards; the pips are the printed suit symbols, which picture cards do not show. To give someone the pip is British slang for annoying them.
explanation.definitionFit: Kings, queens and jacks are picture cards and count among bridge honours, yet carry no pips.

clue.text: Element, one strengthening teeth – oddly easy to replace lack, likewise

indicators.note: oddly means taking the letters in odd-numbered positions
to replace means one set of letters is swapped in for another

blocks.note: calcium is the mineral that strengthens teeth
the first and third letters of this word
the first and third letters of this word

explanation.surface: A chemist names an element that strengthens teeth, noting an easy replacement for something lacking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'likewise' says 'lack' is treated oddly too, giving the letters swapped out of the mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesium is a soft alkali metal, a chemical element with symbol Cs.

clue.text: Man didn't quite swallow one piece of bread

indicators.note: not quite doing something means falling short, so the final letter is cut

blocks.note: a chap is a man
to swallow is to eat, past tense ate
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man couldn't quite get a piece of bread down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallow' looks like a container signal but gives a verb meaning eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is an Indian flatbread, so a piece of bread.

clue.text: Nearly a colour match

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is cut

blocks.note: taken as written
green is a colour

explanation.surface: Two shades almost match in colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that agree correspond or tally, which is what it means for them to match.

clue.text: Gunners picking themselves up on the ways back

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads from bottom to top
back means the word is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the gunners themselves: RA is the Royal Artillery
lanes are ways or roads

explanation.surface: Soldiers pick themselves up off the roads after a retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is the London football club nicknamed the Gunners; 'themselves' points back to gunners, the Royal Artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal Football Club's nickname is the Gunners, from its origins at the Royal Arsenal munitions works.

clue.text: After clearing out rubbish, order transport in regular form

indicators.note: clearing out the inside of a word leaves only its outer letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of this word
the OM is the Order of Merit
a bus is a form of transport

explanation.surface: After a clear-out of junk, someone orders a vehicle of the usual kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhombus is a quadrilateral with all four sides equal, a regular geometric shape.

clue.text: One way to maintain vigour in the country

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold, so one piece keeps another within it

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Rd is the abbreviation for road, a way
élan is dash or vigour

explanation.surface: Advice on one way to keep up your energy in rural parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the country' looks like the countryside, but it is a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland is a nation, so a country.

clue.text: The most intense part of section 8?

blocks.note: dept is short for department, a section
H is the eighth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A question about the busiest bit of a legal or bureaucratic section numbered eight.
explanation.definitionFit: The depth of winter or despair is its most extreme part, as in the depths of winter.

clue.text: Exeunt, trousers perhaps not wanted

blocks.note: first meaning: the actors leave the stage, read as players going off
second meaning: discarded clothing handed on

explanation.walkthrough: Exeunt is the stage direction for several characters leaving; read the first meaning as the company of actors heading off.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase splits into players exiting the stage and clothes thrown away as unwanted.

clue.text: In Paradise Lost, say, pressure on pair oddly missing a piece of fruit

indicators.note: with the odd-placed letters gone, only the even-placed ones remain
in an across clue, one thing on another comes after it, so the first-named piece goes second

blocks.note: Milton's Paradise Lost is an epic poem
the second and fourth letters of this word
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: In Milton's poem, temptation by a piece of fruit puts pressure on the first couple.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' places the first piece after the second, so pressure follows the remnant of pair.
explanation.definitionFit: The epicarp is the outer skin of a fruit, a botanical part of it.

clue.text: After training I belong in base

indicators.note: training reshapes something, so the letters are worked into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A recruit, having finished training, feels at home on the military base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' reads as a military base but is the adjective meaning low.
explanation.definitionFit: Base and ignoble are synonyms meaning dishonourable or morally low.

clue.text: Moans with blemish turning into utter mess

indicators.note: turning means the letters change around into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of both words to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Complaints about a flaw escalate into total chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: Omnishambles was coined in the British political satire The Thick of It.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnishambles is a situation mishandled in every possible way, a complete shambles.
